Counting continues amid dispute

Officials say the final result may take several more days to confirm.

Counting of ballots continued on Wednesday in the capital as rival parties traded accusations over irregularities at several polling stations, delaying the announcement of official results.

The electoral commission said it had received 41 formal complaints, of which 12 had been dismissed after review and the rest remained under investigation by a panel of independent judges.

International observers described the voting itself as orderly, but noted that long queues and late-opening stations had disadvantaged voters in the eastern provinces.

Analysts expect the margin between the two leading candidates to be narrow, which could trigger a recount in the most closely contested constituencies later this week.
